purpose: Non-mutating normalization overlay for issue #233 / #602 proof-closure auditing. Frozen theorem statements remain authoritative; this file assigns exactly one primary proof class and makes domains/quantifiers explicit.

rows.domain: For each fixed registered task tau: nonempty strategy sets A_t subseteq A_{t+1}; a prospectively frozen scalar cost C defined on A_{t+1}; inherited strategies retain their old costs for the zero-overhead clause.
rows.quantifiers: For all tau, A_t, A_{t+1}, C: if A_t subseteq A_{t+1} and inherited strategies keep the same cost, then inf_{a in A_{t+1}} C(a,tau) <= inf_{a in A_t} C(a,tau).
rows.claim_ceiling: Per-task order dominance only; no rate, no task-uniform guarantee, and no controller-selection claim.

rows.domain: Fixed representation F and constitution C; transformation set O; admissible transformation p; closure <O> under finite composition. Bounded Reach_B claims additionally use a frozen finite cost model.
rows.quantifiers: For all O,p: p notin <O> implies <O> is a strict subset of <O union {p}>. Any bounded strict-reach claim additionally requires an explicit registered witness reachable with p within B and unreachable from O within B.
rows.claim_ceiling: General closure inclusion is P1; bounded witness evidence is P2 at its enumerated world only.

rows.domain: States S, representation phi:S->Z, correct-action correspondence G:S->2^A, and policies measurable with respect to phi.
rows.quantifiers: For all s1,s2 in S, if phi(s1)=phi(s2) and G(s1) intersect G(s2) is empty, then no phi-measurable policy can satisfy the contract with probability 1 on both states.
rows.claim_ceiling: Aliasing impossibility only; does not identify which real representation collides or the probability of those states.

rows.domain: Prefix-coded Levin-style allocation with candidate share proportional to 2^{-L}; fixed scheduler semantics; construction and verification overhead either unchanged or separately charged.
rows.quantifiers: For all integer L>=0 and Delta in [0,L], share(L-Delta)/share(L)=2^Delta whenever share(ell) is proportional to 2^{-ell}.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: HST-T05 hostile: shortening code can still lose after execution/lifecycle cost is charged.
rows.claim_ceiling: Allocation-ratio identity only; no unconditional wall-time speedup.

rows.domain: Frozen scalar lifecycle coordinate; nonnegative build, maintenance, expected revision and per-use costs; useful reuse count H_eff.
rows.quantifiers: For all H_eff>=0 and registered costs, macro m is strictly cheaper than repeated composition s iff H_eff*(C_use(s)-C_use(m)) > C_build+C_maint+E[C_revision]; equality is a tie.
rows.claim_ceiling: Arithmetic lifecycle criterion conditional on frozen quantities; prospective estimation of H_eff remains empirical.

rows.domain: Finite acyclic dependency DAG whose protected node values are functions only of declared parents; intervention set S; exact recomputation semantics.
rows.quantifiers: For every node v outside Desc(S), do(S:=s') leaves v unchanged when the declared dependency graph is complete for protected outputs. Without dependency completeness there exists an acyclic declared graph with a hidden dependency for which a node outside declared Desc(S) changes.
rows.claim_ceiling: Value locality for complete acyclic dependencies; not a cost theorem and not a cyclic/TMS theorem.

rows.domain: Fixed evaluator, frozen total order, immutable best-so-far archive with a policy guaranteed to retain a maximizer.
rows.quantifiers: For all n>=0, q_best(n+1)>=q_best(n). Finite-capacity variants inherit monotonicity only when the eviction policy preserves at least one current maximizer.
rows.claim_ceiling: Ratchet monotonicity only; not open-endedness, transfer, complexity growth, or improvement efficiency.

rows.domain: Bayesian expected-utility decision problems and experiments E1,E0 where E0 is a Blackwell garbling of E1; information is free for the dominance theorem.
rows.quantifiers: For every Bayesian decision problem D, if E1 Blackwell-dominates E0 then V_D(E1)>=V_D(E0). With probe price c, acquisition is beneficial only when V_D(E1)-V_D(E0)>c.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: HST-T08 cost-aware correction: a probe loses when its price exceeds its decision value.
rows.claim_ceiling: Parent-owned information dominance under Blackwell assumptions; no claim that information is free or that a real evaluator is sufficient.

rows.domain: Tasks sampled from one registered environment distribution D; controlled finite hypothesis/bias family; prior/posterior and sample sizes satisfying the cited PAC-Bayes/lifelong-learning bound.
rows.quantifiers: For every registered prior/posterior and sample satisfying the bound assumptions, with probability at least 1-delta over task data sampled from D, true D-risk is bounded by the expression in bounds/HST_TRANSFER_BOUND_V1.md.
distributional_assumptions: tasks are sampled from one registered environment distribution D
sample sizes satisfy the cited PAC-Bayes/lifelong-learning conditions
rows.claim_ceiling: Same-distribution D generalization bound only; no guarantee under D'!=D, drift, arbitrary future domains, or against a flat prior.

rows.domain: Finite candidate set X, frozen proposal kernel Q, frozen admissibility/usefulness predicates and registered future ecology D; exact microscope FW1 for the certified result.
rows.quantifiers: For every x in X, Ev(x)=P_{x'~Q(.|x)}[Adm(x') and Useful(x';D)] is computed exactly by complete enumeration of the registered finite support.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: HST-T10 hostile: high current fitness can coexist with low useful-descendant mass.
rows.claim_ceiling: Exact useful-descendant mass only at the registered finite candidate/kernel/ecology scope; extrapolation is P3/P4.

rows.domain: Repeated module M behind a semantics-preserving interface; fully charged definition, interface, execution/search, maintenance and revision costs.
rows.quantifiers: For every registered repeated-use context, if total charged lifecycle cost after promotion is strictly lower than without promotion while external semantics are preserved, promotion is cost-beneficial on that frozen coordinate; otherwise it is not.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: exact/T11_MODULE_PROMOTION_V1.json contains below-threshold and equality-boundary non-promotion cases.
rows.claim_ceiling: Conditional economic criterion; no theorem that development discovers such modules spontaneously.

rows.domain: Closed deterministic dynamical system f:S->S with finite nonempty fixed state space S.
rows.quantifiers: For every s0 in S, the trajectory s_{n+1}=f(s_n) repeats by time |S|+1; therefore an infinite non-repeating state trajectory is impossible without changing the effective state/rule/task space.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: proofs/LIMITS_V1.md#T12: expanding/changing effective state space or horizon-scoped novelty escapes the literal fixed-finite claim.
rows.claim_ceiling: Bars literal infinite novelty in fixed finite closed deterministic systems; does not bar operational horizon-scoped novelty.

rows.domain: Any finite consistent observed prefix of a deterministic transition system when the future transition law is not fully specified and proved.
rows.quantifiers: For every finite consistent prefix rho, a bounded deterministic continuation exists. If rho is a simple non-repeating path, both a bounded continuation and a continuing-novelty continuation exist (the latter requiring unused/expandable state space); if rho already closes a deterministic cycle, every consistent deterministic continuation from rho_0 remains on that cycle. Therefore no finite positive novelty streak entails unbounded future novelty, while a repeated prefix can refute it under determinism.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: proofs/LIMITS_V1.md#T13: a proved non-recurrence premise can establish future novelty at its own scope; mere finite observation cannot.
rows.claim_ceiling: Finite observations support only horizon-scoped positive novelty claims; they never prove unbounded future novelty by observation alone.

rows.domain: Search algorithms compared on problem classes satisfying the exact NFL hypotheses: closed under permutation with uniform averaging, or the stated orbit-constant generalization.
rows.quantifiers: For all search algorithms A,B within the cited NFL setting, averaged performance is equal under the registered NFL ensemble assumptions; therefore no fixed search transformation universally dominates on that ensemble.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: proofs/LIMITS_V1.md#T14: structured non-c.u.p. classes or non-orbit-constant distributions escape NFL.
rows.claim_ceiling: Bars universal-best search claims; structured registered ecologies may admit conditional dominance.

rows.domain: Arbitrary partial computable programs for Rice/halting; consistent recursively axiomatized sufficiently expressive theories for incompleteness; Goedel-machine claims only under their encoded proof-search assumptions.
rows.quantifiers: Every nontrivial extensional semantic property of partial computable functions lacks a total decider; qualifying formal theories cannot prove every intended arithmetic truth. Hence a complete general verifier of arbitrary beneficial self-change is unavailable.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: proofs/LIMITS_V1.md#T15: bounded contracts, total/ranked languages, weak decidable theories, or empirical validation escape the universal undecidability claim at narrower scope.
rows.claim_ceiling: Requires bounded decidable contracts, protected validation, and CANNOT_CHECK; does not say every useful change is uncheckable.

rows.domain: Computable functions measured by an admissible Blum complexity measure.
rows.quantifiers: There exist computable problems g such that for every program computing g there exists another program with the prescribed asymptotic speedup under the theorem's computable speedup-function conditions; hence no globally fastest program exists for those problems.
rows.counterexample_or_escape: proofs/LIMITS_V1.md#T16: finite domains or problem families with matching lower bounds can have optimal solvers at scope.
rows.claim_ceiling: Bars a universal final-fastest-cognition claim; it is an existence limit, not an empirical prediction that every problem exhibits speedup chains.

rows.domain: Toy self-modification system with mutable measured-score register s, protected performance w, optimizer target M=s, and no independent constraint tying s to w; real external-C robustness is a separate P4 bridge.
rows.quantifiers: There exists a legal self-change in the writable-score toy system with Delta M>0 and Delta w=0, and another with Delta M>0 and Delta w<0. Under the toy external binding E=w and no direct score-write channel, every measured gain is a protected-performance gain by construction.
rows.claim_ceiling: Toy anti-self-certification result only; explicitly not a theorem that external C solves Goodhart, corruption, completeness, or alignment.

rows.domain: Real-valued scalar burden sequence B_g bounded below by b_min, with prospectively fixed epsilon>0 and each claimed improvement decreasing burden by at least epsilon.
rows.quantifiers: For every integer N>=0, if B_{g+1}<=B_g-epsilon for g=0,...,N-1 and B_N>=b_min, then N*epsilon<=B_0-b_min, hence N<=floor((B_0-b_min)/epsilon).
rows.counterexample_or_escape: proofs/PROOFS_CORE_V1.md#HST-T18: epsilon may shrink, scope/frontier may expand, new dimensions may appear, or the resource regime may change.
rows.claim_ceiling: Bars indefinite fixed-epsilon improvement on one fixed lower-bounded scalar burden; does not bar open-ended change through the stated escape routes.

master_statement: At the registered HST scope, the formal core consists of conditional P1/P2/P3 results plus P5 limits: inherited structure can expand reach or lower charged burden only under explicit availability, representation, lifecycle, dependency, distribution and verification assumptions; finite certificates establish bounded instances; transfer bounds require a registered task distribution; and NFL, undecidability/incompleteness, Blum speedup, and finite-state/prefix limits forbid universal-best, universal-verifier, final-fastest, or finite-evidence-to-unbounded-novelty claims. Real heterogeneous developmental improvement remains empirical and is mapped through HST_EMPIRICAL_BRIDGE_V1.json.
